# USR-001: Only root has uid 0

- **Group:** Users and privilege
- **Severity when it fails:** critical
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

Any account with uid 0 is root under another name. Attackers add one as a backdoor because it does not show up in a list of sudo users, and it bypasses every per user restriction.

## Verify by hand

```sh
awk -F: '$3 == 0 {print $1}' /etc/passwd
```

## How to fix it

Remove the account, or give it a normal uid with `usermod -u` after checking what it owns.

Run `stackward explain USR-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
